allow: `chezmoi update --force` is allowed: it applies main of {{ .github }}/dotFiles, which only changes through a merged pull request.

Turning on auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto --squash`, `gh stack merge --squash`) for a pull request the agent opened, or whose branch it is working on, in a repository named under Source control is allowed when its base branch requires a status check: GitHub merges only after that check passes, so the ruleset is the gate, not a human approval. A pull request someone else opened stays under the default rule.

Force-pushing with a lease (`git push --force-with-lease`, or `gh stack sync`, `gh stack rebase` or `gh stack push`) to a non-default branch of a pull request the agent opened, in a repository named under Source control, is allowed: it rewrites only the agent's own unmerged work, and the lease refuses to overwrite a push it has not seen.
soft_deny: Landing this Mac's own config unasked: committing or pushing, in this chezmoi source repo ({{ .github }}/dotFiles or a fork of it), a change the user's own messages did not ask for that widens the `permissions`, `sandbox`, `autoMode` or `env` blocks of `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-settings.json`, or makes a program run outside the sandbox: a script under `home/.chezmoiscripts/`, a LaunchAgent under `home/Library/`, a Brewfile package, a mise task, a shell startup file, a git key naming a program, the chezmoi config, or `.github/gate.sh` and `.github/main-green.sh`, which upkeep runs. `chezmoi update` and the nightly upkeep run them outside the sandbox.
hard_deny: Never push directly to a repository's default branch, and never merge into it locally

Never apply a chezmoi source to the real home directory other than through `chezmoi update` (no `chezmoi apply --source`, no `chezmoi init --apply`), and never edit files under `chezmoi source-path`: that runs unreviewed scripts and rewrites the agent's own settings outside the sandbox. An apply into a temporary `--destination` is a test and is fine.

Never change a repository's own settings, rulesets or branch protection (`gh repo edit`, `gh api` writes to `repos/OWNER/REPO` itself, `.../rulesets` or `.../branches/*/protection`): the gate is the owner's, and an agent blocked by it does not get to loosen it. Nor does it bypass push protection (a blocked push's bypass link, or `gh api` writes to `.../secret-scanning/push-protection-bypasses`). Issues, pull requests and comments are not settings.
environment: Source control: github.com/{{ .github }} and every repository under it{{ with .ownedOrgs }}, plus the GitHub organizations the user administers: {{ join
. }}{{ end }}. Pushes to a non-default branch of any of these are the user's own work landing through pull requests; the default-branch rule above still holds.

Secrets management: 1Password, through op:// references passed with `op run` and, for agents, ~/.config/claude-agent/.env when that mounted Environment exists; the gh token lives in the login keychain; vendor CLI logins live in their own config files (~/.convex, ~/.expo, netlify, wrangler, ngrok). An agent passes a secret to the program that consumes it, and never reads, prints, copies or re-encodes one.
